newsitem.title: LEBANON: $90 mln raised for renovation of two Beirut hotels.
newsitem.headline: $90 mln raised for renovation of two Beirut hotels.

text.p: A Beirut bank and an investment house announced on Tuesday the finalisation of a $90-million debt and equity package for the restoration of two prime Beirut hotels damaged in the 1975-90 civil war.

The deal to finance the reconstruction of the Phoenicia and Vendome hotels comprised $45 million in a syndicated loan from Lebanese and foreign banks and institutions, $35 million in privately-placed equity and a $10-million direct loan.

The 572-room Phoenicia, one of Beirut's pre-war grand hotels, and the luxury, 96-room Vendome stand close to the seafront in the hotels district that was the heart of Lebanon's flourishing pre-war tourist industry.
Fransabank, lead manager for the debt financing, finalised the operation in cooperation with Beirut investment house, Lebanon Invest, which also structured the equity part.

The German Investment and Development Company (DEG), which has a stake in Fransabank, provided $10 million in a separate loan to Societe des Grands Hotels du Liban (SGHL), which owns Phoenicia and a has a major stake in the firm that owns Vendome.

"We finalised the financing operation together with Lebanon Invest, and with the contribution of our partners in Fransabank, D.E.G., and with the participation of Lebanese, Arab and foreign banks and institutions," Fransabank President and Director General Adnan Kassar told a news conference in Beirut.

Lebanon Invest Chairman Marwan Ghandour told Reuters the deal took a long time to finalise -- it was first announced in December -- as much legal work was needed and a 17-day Israeli blitz in April caused a "period of uncertainty about things".
But Kassar said the operation was completed despite negative publicity from the Israeli onslaught against Hizbollah guerrillas in Lebanon, as the talks were in progress.
"We did not back down from the financing step and none of the institutions that shared with us this step backed down," Kassar added.

Banks involved in the debt financing include Berlin-based Berliner Bank and Lebanese banks Banque Audi, Bank of Beirut and the Arab Countries, Banque Saradar, Banque Beyrouth Pour Le Commerce and Credit Libanais.
Beirut-based Arab Finance Company and Kuwait-based Public Institution for Social Security also took part.
Ghandour said that about $31 million of the equity deal was in a private share placement with Lebanese, Arab and European institutions. The remaining $4 million came from shareholders
He said the bulk of the $80-million debt and equity package, about $65 million, would go towards the restoration of the Phoenicia which is expected to take two years.
Works on the Vendome have neared completion and the hotel is expected to re-open in October, he added.
Ghandour said tender documents have been issued for the Phoenicia refurbishment project and bids were expected to be awarded in October and works to begin by January.
The hotels district was gutted in hand-to-hand sectarian fighting at the start of the war and the hotels were occupied by squatters until the government evicted them at the end of 1995.
